questions.question: Describe the chain of events that starts puberty, from the brain to the changes in the body.
questions.expected_answer: The hypothalamus in the brain signals the pituitary gland, which releases hormones into the blood. These stimulate the gonads (testes or ovaries) to grow, produce gametes and release sex hormones (testosterone, or oestrogen and progesterone). The sex hormones travel in the blood to target organs and bring about the changes of puberty.

questions.question: Name the hormone made by the testes and the two made by the ovaries, and give one effect of each.
questions.expected_answer: Testes: testosterone, e.g. deepening of the voice, growth of facial hair, muscle development or start of sperm production. Ovaries: oestrogen, e.g. breast development, widening of the hips or thickening of the uterine lining; progesterone, which maintains the thickened uterine lining and supports pregnancy.

questions.question: List two secondary sexual characteristics found only in boys, two found only in girls and two found in both.
questions.expected_answer: Boys: e.g. facial hair, deeper voice, broader shoulders, more muscle. Girls: e.g. breast development, wider hips, menstruation. Both: e.g. pubic and underarm hair, growth spurt, active sweat glands and body odour, oily skin and acne, emotional changes.
